description: Rewrite measures from..to (numbers, inclusive) of ONE track of the draft with .cesure measures, as read_score returns them; to = from - 1 inserts before from. A measure written with its id stays that measure, even rewritten; one written without its id is a new measure, and the one it stood for is removed with what it carried (a repeat it opened, say). A measure of the range left out is removed, and measures [] removes the whole range. The other tracks follow column by column, as in the editor: a column is inserted, removed or given a time signature on every track; its repeat signs are carried as the editor carries them, and a tempo change stays on its column (on the next one when its column is removed), so no other column changes tempo. A note may be written by its pitch (E4, Bb3) in place of fret.string: Cesure chooses its string and fret, and never moves a note written with its string. The answer names the measures written. A written measure that does not read or does not fill its time signature refuses the whole call, the refusal naming each fault with its place; a measure sent back unchanged (same id and content) is kept as it was. Measure notation (.cesure): each voice is one string of beats separated by spaces. beat = content.duration[{d | tu 3}]; content = fret.string[{note props}] | pitch | (note note …) | r. Durations, on EVERY beat: 1 whole, 2 half, 4 quarter, 8, 16, 32, 64. Strings from 1 (the highest); x as fret mutes. A pitch (C4 = middle C, F#3, Bb2) lets Cesure choose string and fret; a staff is all by pitch or all fret.string. Beat props: d dotted, tu 3 triplet on each beat of the group. Note props: t tie, h hammer/pull-off and sl slide to the next note on that string, v vibrato, b (0 4) a whole-tone bend. EACH VOICE FILLS ITS TIME SIGNATURE EXACTLY: 4/4 = 4 quarters = 8 eighths, 3/4 = 3 quarters, 6/8 = 6 eighths; rests complete a short one. A measure without numerator/denominator is 4/4, whatever came before. A second voice (a bass under a melody) is a second string in voices. Examples (4/4): "5.3.4 7.3.4 r.2" (fret 5 then 7 on string 3 (strings from 1, the highest), quarters; a half rest); "(0.1 1.2 0.3).2 x.6.4 r.4" (a chord, a half; a muted note); "E4.8 F#4.8 G4.4 Bb3.2" (notes by pitch (C4 = middle C): Cesure chooses string and fret); "5.3.4{d} 5.3.8 2.1.8{tu 3} 3.1.8{tu 3} 5.1.8{tu 3} 7.2{h}.8 8.2.8" (dotted quarter; a triplet of eighths (each beat carries it); a hammer-on to the next note); "5.3.2 5.3{t}.4 7.2{sl}.8 9.2{v}.8" (a tie to the note before, a slide, a vibrato). A measure: {"id":"p2","numerator":3,"denominator":4,"staves":[{"voices":["0.1.8 2.1.8 3.1.4 5.1.4","0.6.2{d}"]}]}. The full format: https://cesure.app/format
